Alpha install

From the release wheels to a logged-in administrator who can create a project and a prompt: install, migrate, start MLflow, configure roles and providers, verify.

DeveloperOperatorTutorialBETA
PrerequisitesPython 3.10, 3.11 or 3.12 and the three CALIBER wheels (release assets or a source checkout)
Reviewed 2026-10-13 · 0.1.0a1 alpha

This page takes you from nothing to a logged-in administrator who can create a project and a prompt. It needs no Docker and no repository checkout. Every command here is executed by scripts/verify-alpha-install.sh, so if a step stops working the check fails before you do.

CALIBER is alpha software. The packages are not on PyPI yet, so pip install caliber-sdk returns "no matching distribution". Install from the wheels instead.

What you get#

PieceWhere it runs
CALIBER (the control plane and API)uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:5001
MLflow (the prompt registry)mlflow server on 127.0.0.1:5000, its own SQLite file
CALIBER's databaseone SQLite file, separate from MLflow's

The LLM and the evaluator are simulated in this setup. That is the honest offline default: calibration runs and returns candidates, but the evaluation scores are canned and every screen that shows them says so. See Real LLM and evaluation to change that.

1. Get the wheels#

Download caliber_sdk, caliber_cli and caliber_suite (all 0.1.0a1) from the release assets into a wheels/ directory. From a source checkout you can build them instead:

python3.12 -m venv build-venv && build-venv/bin/pip install build
for pkg in sdk/caliber-sdk sdk/caliber-cli caliber; do
  build-venv/bin/python -m build --wheel --outdir wheels "$pkg"
done

A wheel built this way has no bundled web UI. The release wheel does.

2. Create a virtual environment and install#

Python 3.13 is not supported yet. Use 3.10, 3.11 or 3.12.

python3.12 -m venv alpha
source alpha/bin/activate
pip install --find-links ./wheels caliber-sdk caliber-cli caliber-suite

3. Migrate the database#

The server never creates its own tables. Run the migration before the first start, and after every upgrade:

export CALIBER_DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///$PWD/caliber.db
caliber-migrate

Without this step the server starts and /health looks fine, but every login fails with no such table: caliber_user_accounts. caliber-migrate works from any directory and never prints the database URL.

4. Start MLflow#

In a second terminal, with the same virtual environment active:

mlflow server \
  --backend-store-uri sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db \
  --default-artifact-root $PWD/mlflow-artifacts \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5000

Keep MLflow on its own SQLite file. Sharing one file with CALIBER works, but SQLite allows one writer at a time, and the server warns at startup if you do.

5. Configure and start CALIBER#

The server reads its configuration from the process environment. It does not read a .env file.

export MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://127.0.0.1:5000
export CALIBER_ADMIN_USERS=admin
export CALIBER_OPERATOR_USERS=admin
export CALIBER_APPROVER_USERS=admin
export CALIBER_PROMOTER_PROVIDER=mlflow
export CALIBER_ARTIFACT_STORE_PROVIDER=mlflow
export CALIBER_EVAL_PROVIDER=fake
export CALIBER_LOG_SINK=stderr
export CALIBER_AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=false
export CALIBER_AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOW_INSECURE_DEFAULT=true
uvicorn caliber.server:create_app --factory --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5001

What each group does:

  • Roles. An account holds a password only. CALIBER_ADMIN_USERS, CALIBER_OPERATOR_USERS and CALIBER_APPROVER_USERS decide what that user may do. Leave all three empty and the first login is a viewer who cannot create a project. The server logs an error when that happens.
  • Providers. The promoter and artifact store are the real MLflow ones, so Apply changes the registry. CALIBER_EVAL_PROVIDER=fake is written out so the simulated evaluator is a choice you can see.
  • Bootstrap login. With the last two lines, the first start creates one account, admin with password admin. They are for a machine only you can reach. Change the password under Administration straight away, and never carry these lines into a network-reachable deployment. With neither a password source nor these lines, no account is created and the server logs a warning saying nobody can log in.

6. Verify#

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5001/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/readiness

Expect "ready":true. The simulated list should contain at most llm and eval. If it lists promoter or artifact_store, the release path is simulated and Apply will not change MLflow.

Then sign in and create a project:

B=http://127.0.0.1:5001/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber
curl -s -c jar -X POST $B/auth/login -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"user_id":"admin","password":"admin"}'
curl -s -b jar $B/auth/session                  # "is_admin": true
curl -s -b jar -X POST $B/projects -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"my-first-project"}'
curl -s -b jar -X POST $B/prompts -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"my-first-prompt","template":"Answer briefly: {{question}}"}'

With a release wheel, open http://127.0.0.1:5001/caliber/ and sign in as admin / admin.

Real LLM and evaluation#

Evidence you can trust needs a real evaluator and a real model. Install the extra, set the key, and switch both providers:

pip install --find-links ./wheels "caliber-suite[llm]"
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
export CALIBER_LLM_PROVIDER=openai
export CALIBER_LLM_API_KEY_ENV=OPENAI_API_KEY
export CALIBER_EVAL_PROVIDER=mlflow

Restart CALIBER. /readiness then lists nothing under simulated. A real model with the fake evaluator is refused at startup unless you set CALIBER_ALLOW_SIMULATED_PROVIDERS=true.

Docker instead#

If you would rather run the whole stack in containers, use make start from a source checkout. The container entrypoint runs the migration and sets the roles and providers for you. See Local bring-up.

Check it yourself#

From a source checkout, this script runs the steps above in a scratch directory and fails if any of them stops working:

scripts/verify-alpha-install.sh --python python3.12
# or against downloaded release wheels:
scripts/verify-alpha-install.sh --wheel-dir ./wheels

If something is wrong#

SymptomCauseFix
/readiness is not ready with a schema blocker, or login returns 500 and the log says no such tablethe migration never ran, or the database is behind this releaserun caliber-migrate with the same CALIBER_DATABASE_URL and restart
Login works but "create project" is refused with 403no role list names youset CALIBER_ADMIN_USERS and restart
admin/admin is rejectedno account was createdset the two bootstrap lines in step 5, or a password source, on a fresh database
/readiness lists promotera fake promoter was configuredset CALIBER_PROMOTER_PROVIDER=mlflow
pip install caliber-sdk finds nothingthe packages are not on PyPIinstall from the wheels as in step 2
